q: 1. How many bird species are currently recorded in Nepal?
explain: The 904th species is the Collared Kingfisher. It was first seen at Janakpurdham, Dhanusha on B.S. 2083 Asoj 13. It is found mainly in coastal areas. Scientific name: Todiramphus chloris. The species is found mainly in South Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and Pacific coastal regions, and its nearest permanent habitat is West Bengal in India and the Sundarbans of Bangladesh. Ornithologists estimate that in Nepal it arrived by wandering along the Ganga–Brahmaputra river system or by losing its way due to weather.

q: 2. Which approach is typically adopted by states to manage population growth in urban areas under planned development?
options: Building affordable housing and improving infrastructure
Ignoring the need for urban development
explain: States manage urban growth by proactively planning for affordable housing and infrastructure to prevent the rise of slums and chaotic sprawl.

q: 3. What is the Baby Boom related to?
options: A surge in the birth of children
explain: Shortly after the Second World War ended, from 1948 onwards, an unprecedented number of children were born worldwide, at a rate never seen before. Demographers called this event of rising births the 'Baby Boom'. It lasted about 12 years, until 1960. The baby boom was greatest especially in the post-war regions of Europe, America, Japan and Korea.

q: 4. Who is the mountaineer who succeeded in climbing all 14 mountains in the world above eight thousand meters at the youngest age and entering the Guinness Book of World Records?
explain: Mingma, who first climbed Manaslu in 2022, achieved this feat by 2024.

q: 5. Until when was the practice of writing the tithi and weekday while mentioning dates in documents in Nepal in force?
explain: The practice of writing the tithi and weekday in documents remained in force until B.S. 1961 Magh.

q: 6. According to the Recent study conducted by department of hydrology and metrology, the average maximum temperature of Nepal has risen by ----------
explain: Studies by the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) indicate an annual increase in maximum temperature of about 0.056°C in Nepal.

q: 7. Which of the following Greenhouse Gases has the highest atmospheric lifetime?
explain: Sulphur Hexafluoride (SF6) is extremely stable and can remain in the atmosphere for over 3,000 years.

q: 8. When was Kalapathar meeting at foothill of Mt. Everest held to draw the attention of the world regarding the effect of Climate Change?
explain: The Nepal Cabinet held a historic meeting at Kalapathar (5,542m) on December 4, 2009 (Mangsir 19, 2066).

q: 9. Which is the nation to conduct the Cabinet Meeting under the water to gain the attention of the world to reduce the effect of climate change?
explain: The Maldives held an underwater cabinet meeting in 2009 to highlight the threat of rising sea levels to the island nation.

q: 10. Which international organization has declared a global climate & environmental emergency?
explain: The European Parliament declared a 'climate and environmental emergency' in Europe and globally in November 2019.

q: 11. When was the National Climate Change Policy introduced in Nepal?
explain: The revised National Climate Change Policy was approved in 2076 B.S. (2019), replacing the previous 2067 policy.
